avis.titre: I love other Paula's Choice products (I exclusively use PC AHA/BHA ...
avis.texte: I love other Paula's Choice products (I exclusively use PC AHA/BHA and retinol), so I was both surprised and disappointed to find this product consistently abysmal. I have now ordered this product three times (in the sample size each time, as Vitamin C in L-AA form degrades quickly following exposure to light/air)-- once directly from the PC website, and twice through Amazon. Each time, this product was already bright amber in color (including the time I ordered directly from the PC website), indicating late stages of oxidation. This also smells bad, as other reviewers have noted (kind of like hot dog water)-- some of that is just because vitamin C smells, but some of that is due to the fact that the product was spoiled. L-AA, of course, degrades quickly, and some oxidation is more or less inevitable unless you're formulating your own vitamin C products at home. However, this is theoretically stabilized by ferulic acid and tocopherol, so I don't understand why the product was at such late stages of oxidation each time I received it, and as a result I'm concerned they're not doing effective quality control or tracking sell-by dates. Moreover, it's fairly damning that this is packaged in an eyedropper bottle, especially since part of the Paula's Choice Gospel is packaging, and this packaging is dreadful. Bottom line: this product is either worthless or actively harmful. At this price point, that's ridiculous.

I see some reviews talk about issues with packaging and spills but I've personally never had an issue with any of that so, it might depend on location or how far the package is being sent. And for anyone concerned about the product being different colors when you order a new replacement, that's just how this product works! Visit Paula's Choice website or google about the product. There's actually a variation of different colors this product can be and still be safe to use. Vitamin C is finicky like that. Another warning is be careful what else you mix this with and how you layer it with other products. Looking at all the reviews I am curious how many novice skincare folks are buying this product not realizing that vitamin C is an acid. avis.titre: Reliable travel size trio with some standout pieces
avis.texte: Paula's Choice is a standout brand for skincare products that I've come to love, so I jumped at the chance to try this set out. All three bottles arrived cleanly sealed, and the small travel‑friendly sizes actually made it easier for me to see how they layered without dealing with full‑size packaging. The mandelic and lactic acid exfoliant has a thin, almost watery texture that spreads quickly with fingertips. I noticed a mild scent at first that faded fast, and it felt gentle even on the more reactive areas around my nose. It didn’t create overnight changes, but it kept my skin smooth without dryness. The C15 booster was the product I focused on the most because vitamin C serums can be hit or miss for me. This one absorbed fast and gave my skin a soft, slightly brighter feel the next morning. The smell is not my favorite, a bit sharp and chemical, but it disappears once it sinks in. The SPF 50 moisturizer surprised me the most. It is very fluid, almost runny, so I had to shake the bottle well. It blended in easily and did not sting or pill up. Overall, this kit feels thoughtfully formulated and easy to use, although the fragrance and small sizes may not appeal to everyone. For checking product compatibility or building a simple brightening routine, it worked well for me.

I was going out of town and this seemed like a great travel item for my skincare routine. The product itself is good. I've used a Vitamin C serum for a long time, and this one is good. The percentage of Vitamin C is lower than the one I currently use. So I didn't experience any burning and didn't need to ease into using it daily. I really liked the suncreen. It too didn't irritate my skin. The exfoliate was good as well. I don't use an exfoliate as I use a face cleaning pad that exfoliates every time I wash my face. This was nice, but I think the exfoliating pad I use, is why this made my face sting slightly. I think the product is a good product. I love that it is travel size. My issue is the price point for this item.

Paula’s Choice Brighter Days Ahead skin care kit resurfaces skin with effective ingredients to gently exfoliate skin, improve sun damage, dullness, fine lines and reverses a compromised skin barrier. Step 1: The first step is to apply the exfoliant that includes a timed release AHA complex. This product alone is worth the price of admission! Apply a thin layer over skin and leave on. The container has a lock down lid under the cap to protect the efficacy of the ingredients. Step 2: Apply the C15 Super Booster with 15% Vitamin C, Vitamin E and Ferulic Acid. Use this unscented serum on its own or boost up your moisturizer with several drops. This truly is a super boost of Vitamin C, the Vitamin E and Ferulic also are super antioxidants to nourish skin and reduce fine lines and wrinkles. Step 3: The last step is to add the SPF 50 Sheer Moisturizer with Algae Aminos. This is truly a lightweight, sheer moisturizer that absorbs into skin almost instantly. This is a powerful moisturizer providing the nutrients and protection to round out this brightening kit. All of the products are unscented and powerful. I noticed improved brightening and hydration results immediately after the first use and I expect they will just get better with continued use! If you have sun spots, dullness or your skin needs a reboot, this is the perfect kit to get! I have sensitive skin and experienced no irritation at all.

avis.titre: My skin looks brighter, and has a nice glow.

This kit came very well presented, which would make for a lovely gift idea. I appreciate that all of the products were sealed or wrapped; this is especially important to me when using skincare items. This is a simple 3 step kit, and included different products that are easy to use. The first item is a Mandelic acid exfoliant, which helps to resurface the skin. Next is the C15 Vitamin C booster serum; this comes with an ampoule-style dropper, which is very easy to use. Lastly, is the moisturizer-which includes Vitamin C and SPF 50. I find all of the products to be gentle on my skin, and haven't caused me any issues. I love all of the products included; however, I really like the serum and the moisturizer. I feel that the serum adds a supple effect, while adding a glow. The moisturizer is sheer, and doesn't feel heavy or greasy. All of these skincare items have worked out well for me thus far, though it may take some time to see the longer-term results. I think that this is a nice quality set, and has helped my skin feel smooth and soft. I love the use of vitamin C, as well as the SPF 50 in the moisturizer. These products work well with my skincare routine, as well as my personal needs. I think this is a nice set, and at a decent value for the price point (in my personal opinion). I'm very ple

avis.titre: Fun set for stocking stuffer or travel
avis.texte: This is a great little set of skin care for either travel or to sample. It would also make a great a set for a stocking stuffer or a fun little gift for a gift exchange. The products are all very nice and give you a good understanding of a skin care routine. The “resurface” or exfoliation serum has a bit of a chemical smell but it’s not awful and does dissipate. Both the resurface and brighten step are lightweight and absorbed quickly and then the protect step also absorbed nicely. The base was easy to use with makeup and didn’t cause my makeup to run or slip around. This is a fun little set and work well.

This kit comes with 3 items: C5 SPF 50, 6% Mandelic Acid AHA liquid exfoliant, and C15 Super Booster vitamin C face serum. I am amazed that it healed a sore on my face and made my sagging skin more youthful from just one time use. I am amazed by this product, and I will continue to use it. Update: Later on that evening my face broke out like using retinol. I guess that's why it tells you to space out treatments.

The vitamin C serum is my favorite, it gives my face a healthy glow and has really helped fade dullness over time. It also layers nicely under my moisturizer without feeling sticky. I also love the sunscreen moisturizer, it’s perfect for everyday use. It’s lightweight, not greasy. Plus, it fits easily in my bag, so I can take it anywhere. Overall, this kit is simple, effective, and travel-friendly!

This is a great little kit with some impressive ingredients to resurface and improve skin texture and complexion. The bottles are smaller than I expected (as you can see in the hand comparison) but that actually makes it perfect for traveling while maintaining a solid skincare routine. The exfoliant feels nice on the skin and is very similar to their popular BHA exfoliant. The SPF moisturizer has a slight tint and a lighter, more liquid texture than I anticipated, but it blends in easily and provides good coverage. Overall, I’m really happy with this set so far!

Recently, I started using Paula’s Choice C15 Super Booster, and it's been quite the revelation for my mid-30s skin. Grappling with the usual—dullness, fine lines, and uneven tone—I was keen to see if this product lived up to its hype. And it doesn't disappoint. Even from the first few uses, my skin's more luminous, those fine lines are less pronounced, and my skin's firmness has a newfound bounce to it. Here's the real deal: it's a dream to apply—no stickiness, a subtle scent I adore, and it's incredibly lightweight. I'm layering it right after toning in both my AM and PM routines, and it plays well with my other products—no pilling, just smooth sailing. Being on prescription tretinoin, I've had no irritation adding this to my skincare mix, which is a big win. I've just been using three drops for my face and one for the neck and décolletage, and it's enough to cover all bases. I'm genuinely excited to continue using it and see the long-term effects. If your skin goals align with mine, this booster is definitely worth considering. - xx
